editions.text:
The station logged 214 feeder visits, exceeding the past week's average of 199 and marking a visual rebound from the previous day's quiet 99. While 23 species were recorded, higher than the recent average of 18, the total audio detections fell to 224, below the usual 289. Tufted Titmice dominated the visual count with 99 visits, far outpacing Carolina Chickadees at 41, while Carolina Wrens remained the most vocal presence throughout the day.

A Brown-headed Cowbird was sighted thirteen minutes before sunrise, establishing the first confident visual record at this station. The bird was one of several first-of-the-day species, including an Orchard Oriole, Rose-breasted Grosbeak, and Chimney Swift, all of which appeared only once. These visual events contrasted with the audio log, where no new species were detected for the first time since the microphone change in mid-September.

The shift in audio volume aligns with the replacement of the old seed feeder on September 13, which had caused detection problems, and the switch to the new audio source. Regulars such as the Blue Jay, House Finch, and Northern Cardinal held steady, present every day of the past week.

The yard woke quiet, with a Tufted Titmouse on the tube at 07:06, twelve minutes before the sun cleared the treeline. American Crows were the first voices, their calls filling the 07:00 hour alongside a few Cardinals and Chickadees, while the feeder itself remained sparse until the Chickadees arrived at 07:18.

Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees traded the seed feeder since dawn, each logging over sixty confident visits by the first hour. A female Northern Cardinal perched on the curved metal bar during the rush, and a Ruby-throated Hummingbird appeared at 07:55, the first of seven recorded since.

The audio picture shifted after 08:00 as Carolina Wrens took over, dominating the 09:00 hour with fifty-nine detections. Red-shouldered Hawks have been circling since early, adding four calls to the morning’s soundtrack.

The midday lull is holding steady, with only two species registering any activity in the past hour: a single Carolina Wren call at 15:00 and a Ruby-throated Hummingbird visit at 12:34.

Visits have slowed considerably since the 11:00 hour. The station is running slightly busier than the recent average, with 184 visits logged so far compared to a typical 173.7.

The weather remains warm and still, with no precipitation recorded.

The evening rush pushed the day’s total to 235 visits and 334 audio detections, both figures above recent averages. The 16:00 hour brought the heaviest activity of the late shift, with Carolina Wrens, Chickadees, and Cardinals registering frequent calls and visits.

Tufted Titmice led the visual count at 113, nearly double the 65 logged for Carolina Chickadees. Northern Cardinals rounded out the top three at 14, while Ruby-throated Hummingbirds added 14 visits. The species total of 20 also exceeded the recent average.
